name: Budapest University of Technology and Economics
summary: Budapest technical and economics university: twelve English-taught BSc and single-cycle degrees, entered through its own online tests.

ib.text: No IB points rule: the Diploma counts as your school-leaving certificate and an English-medium school certificate can replace an English test. Entry turns on BME's own online tests.

programmes.name: Civil Engineering
programmes.about: Four-year civil engineering degree in English (240 ECTS) with two specialisations, Structural Engineering and Infrastructure Engineering: bridges, buildings, roads, railways and water works.
programmes.overview: The first years build a base in calculus, physics, mechanics, chemistry and geology, then move into surveying, CAD and BIM, hydraulics, soil mechanics and strength of materials. Core civil subjects follow: construction materials, structural analysis, steel and reinforced concrete structures and foundation engineering, with business law, economics and urban development alongside. A surveying field course gives hands-on practice, and the degree ends with a bachelor thesis. You choose between Structural Engineering (high-rise buildings, halls, frames) and Infrastructure Engineering (roads, railways, water utilities, environmental engineering). Graduates work on bridges, tunnels, power stations, industrial plants and multi-storey buildings.
programmes.selectionNote: Documents pre-screened (school results, motivation letter, activities), then an online Maths and Physics test in English. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Computer Science Engineering
programmes.about: Computer science, algorithms, programming, networks, AI and data security, with two specialisations from semester five: Software Engineering and Infocommunication (210 ECTS).
programmes.overview: The first four semesters share a common foundation of calculus, probability, statistics, algorithms and the theory of computing, together with electronics and physics. Professional subjects then cover digital engineering, computer architecture, communication networks, operating systems, programming in C, C++ and Java, databases, software engineering, computer graphics, artificial intelligence and IT security. From semester five you specialise in either Software Engineering or Infocommunication. An eight-week internship and a thesis project complete the degree. Graduates move into a master's programme or into designing, building and running software and data systems.
programmes.selectionNote: School certificate (70% minimum) pre-screened, then an online Maths and Physics test and a recorded oral test. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Electrical Engineering
programmes.about: Electrical and electronic engineering from power systems to microelectronics, control and programming, with specialisations in embedded and control systems, infocommunication or sustainable energy.
programmes.overview: You start with mathematics, physics and electronic materials, then move into core electrical engineering: microelectronics, electronics, instrumentation, control systems and programming, drawing on both classical and modern methods. The course aims at a balance between theory and practical engineering work. Three specialisations are offered: Embedded and Control Systems, Infocommunication, and Sustainable Electric Energetics. A six-week internship and a thesis project round off the seven semesters. Graduates are prepared for engineering roles in electrical and information technology fields.
programmes.selectionNote: School certificate (70% minimum) pre-screened, then an online Maths and Physics test. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Mechanical Engineering
programmes.about: Mechanics, materials, fluid and thermal sciences and control, combined with laboratory and design work; a broad base for mechanical engineering practice (210 ECTS).
programmes.overview: The programme begins with mathematics (vector algebra, calculus, differential equations) and engineering basics such as physics, technical drawing and machine elements, plus professional English. Later subjects include design and manufacturing, electronics and control, fluids and heat transfer, and materials science, taught with laboratory and design work. You then specialise in Process Engineering (energy processes, fluid systems, CFD, waste management) or Design and Technology (CAD, injection moulding, composites, manufacturing systems). An individual project, an internship and a thesis conclude the degree. Graduates become design engineers, project managers and consultants in automotive, aerospace, energy and manufacturing.
programmes.selectionNote: Documents pre-screened, then an online Maths and Physics test; no oral round. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Vehicle Engineering
programmes.about: Vehicle structures, systems, materials and maintenance, for the automotive industry's shift to new vehicle technologies (210 ECTS).
programmes.overview: The degree opens with mathematics and physics (linear algebra, calculus, probability, statistics, statics and dynamics), then adds the basics of mobility, project work and economics. From there you specialise in one transport area: automotive, vehicle mechatronics, rail vehicles, aircraft, vessels or manufacturing. A thesis project closes the seven semesters. The training covers design, production, testing, maintenance, repair and recycling of transport equipment and vehicle systems. Graduates take up junior engineering tasks in the vehicle industry or continue to a vehicle engineering master's.
programmes.selectionNote: Documents pre-screened, then an online Maths and Physics test; no oral round. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Engineering Management
programmes.about: Engineering plus management: technology, IT, organisation and finance for planning and running technical and economic processes, taught project by project (210 ECTS).
programmes.overview: Engineering and business are taught side by side: mathematics, physics, biology, chemistry and mechanics on one side, business economics, psychology, accounting, statistics and quality management on the other, with materials, transport science, civil engineering and production management in between. The course is strongly project-based, with a project module, a six-week internship and a thesis. In the later semesters you pick a track in Management, Sustainability and Environmental Management, Product Management or Financial Management. Graduates work in quality, service, production, project or environmental management and consulting, or continue to a master's.
programmes.selectionNote: Online test, then an online motivational interview on your interests and why you want the programme. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Professional Pilot
programmes.about: A BSc combined with a commercial pilot licence: flight theory and practical training, ending with multi-crew training in an Airbus A320 simulator environment (210 ECTS).
programmes.overview: Aviation is studied on an engineering base of mathematics, physics, programming, electronics, thermodynamics and fluid dynamics. Aeronautical subjects include the principles of flight, airframes and systems, powerplants, human performance and control systems, followed by navigation, meteorology, flight planning and operations. Flight training runs alongside the theory, ending with multi-crew cooperation training in an Airbus A320 environment, and a thesis is part of the degree. Graduates can hold a commercial pilot licence with a multi-engine instrument rating and go on to first officer or cadet positions with airlines in countries where EASA certificates apply.
programmes.ib: Class 1 EASA medical certificate needed by the end of the first semester, at your own cost; apply with a general medical check.
programmes.selectionNote: Online Maths and Physics test and an oral round; apply with a general medical check. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Physics
programmes.about: Theoretical and experimental physics with mathematics and programming, with a Research Physicist or an Applied Physics specialisation, leading towards the BME Master's (180 ECTS).
programmes.overview: You begin with experimental physics (mechanics, electricity, thermodynamics, modern physics), mathematics, programming and electronics, with a lot of time in laboratory exercises. Later you take theoretical mechanics, quantum mechanics, electrodynamics, statistical physics, optics and solid-state physics. In the final year you choose between a Physicist specialisation, which leans towards theory and programming, and an Applied Physics one, with more lab work and informatics. The thesis involves research with international teams in areas such as quantum physics, nanotechnology, materials, medical physics and data science. Graduates go into research or industries like semiconductors, optics, medical devices, nuclear energy and data analysis.
programmes.selectionNote: Pre-screened on school results; online Maths and Physics test (advanced topics), then an online interview in English. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Physicist-Engineer
programmes.about: Engineering, physics, maths, computing and data science together: quantum and nano technology, photonics, materials, energy and nuclear technology (210 ECTS).
programmes.overview: This course pairs engineering with a stronger natural-science base than most engineering degrees: mechanics, electrodynamics, optics, thermodynamics, condensed matter and statistical physics, together with advanced mathematics. You also learn programming, numerical algorithms and machine learning, plus measurement methods, CAD, electronics and sensing. Specialisations cover nanotechnology and quantum applications, nuclear technologies and sustainable energetics, or scientific data processing. It was developed with industrial partners and includes a six-week internship and a thesis. Graduates move into research and development, data science, AI, energy, medical devices and semiconductors, or on to engineering or physics master's programmes and PhDs.
programmes.selectionNote: Pre-screened on school results; online Maths and Physics test (advanced topics), online interview; 70% admission result needed. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Mathematics
programmes.about: Pure and applied mathematics and mathematical modelling, with project work and a route to research or finance and IT jobs (180 ECTS).
programmes.overview: The first year covers calculus, algebra, geometry and combinatorics, before the course branches into analysis (including differential equations and functional analysis), algebra, differential geometry, discrete mathematics, probability, statistics and operations research. Programming and mathematical modelling run alongside, with accounting and economics courses as a practical side. You choose elective advanced topics, such as numerical methods, stochastics or a research project, and finish with a bachelor thesis. Graduates work in banking, investment, insurance, consulting, data mining and telecommunications, or continue to a master's in mathematics or applied mathematics, and to a PhD.
programmes.selectionNote: Pre-screened on school results; online Maths test (advanced topics) and Physics test, then an oral round. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Chemical Engineering
programmes.about: Analytical, organic and materials chemistry with chemical engineering, maths, physics and economics; specialisation starts in semester five (210 ECTS).
programmes.overview: You build a base in mathematics, physics, general, physical and biochemistry, then move into inorganic and organic chemistry, chemical engineering, chemical technology, environmental technology, analytical chemistry, unit operations and process control. The course combines theory with modern laboratory work, a six-week internship and a thesis. From the fifth semester you choose between chemical and process engineering, industrial pharmaceutics, or materials science. Graduates work in industrial technology, research and development, planning and public administration, or continue to the master's in chemical engineering.
programmes.selectionNote: Online test in Maths plus Chemistry or Physics; no oral round. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Architectural Engineering (single-cycle)
programmes.about: Five-year path straight to a master's in architectural engineering, balancing technical skills (maths and physics) with design; specialise from year four in real estate, sustainable architecture or urban design.
programmes.overview: One continuous degree leads straight to a master's-level qualification, mixing creative and technical training. You practise freehand drawing, visualisation and modelling, work in design studios on housing, public buildings, workplaces and urban design, and study mathematics, statics, structures, building construction, building services, CAAD and BIM, along with architectural history and heritage preservation. From the fourth year you can specialise in Real Estate Development, Sustainable Architecture or Urban Design. A diploma design project and a practice placement finish the course. Graduates enter architectural practice or continue to doctoral study.
programmes.selectionNote: Online Maths and Physics test; maths and/or physics at school recommended; no oral round. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

notes: EU citizens pay the EU column of BME's fee table, lower than the non-EU price for most degrees; Logistics and Transportation Engineering BSc are listed as not offered for 2026/27, so they are left out.
Every BSc applicant sits BME's own online e-admission test (Maths and Physics; Chemical Engineering: Maths plus Chemistry or Physics); practice tests are on the portal.
Applying costs a EUR 150 fee paid by transfer before you submit; BSc applicants must be 18 by enrolment.
